To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Yec loss of a 107-day-old unfed broiler chick is approximately 1.7 kJ per 100 g body weight, and the Yec loss per unit body weight per 100 g of a 107 day-old unfed White Leghorn pullet is approximately 2.3 kJ.

the sex of broiler chicks between 18 and about 107 days of ages does not affect the endogenous and metabolic losses of energy in their voided excrements per unit body weight, but the average losses of energy per unit body weight decrease as the chicks progress in age.

the sex of broiler chicks does not affect the endogenous and metabolic fecal (Yec) energy losses per unit body weight, and that the Yec loss of a chick increases with increases in body weight and decreases with increases in age.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new technique for estimating the energy needs of the growing broiler chick.
the determination of the endogenous energy losses of growing broiler birds.
the development of a new technique for determining the energy requirements for growth of the broiler chicken.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Yec energy losses of the growing broiler chick are influenced by its body weight and BMR energy requirements and that the sex of growing broilers has no effect on their Yec losses.
the age, sex, and body weight of the bird and the strain of the bio-assay bird affect the Yec loss of the bird, but the extent of these variations are not fully understood at present.
the age of broiler chicks and the body weight of rooster influence their Yec losses, but the sex of the animal does not affect its Yec losses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in general, the Yec energy losses of broiler pullets and roosters at different ages are influenced by their BMR energy needs, which are in turn affected by age, body weight, body composition, and strain of birds.
the Yec energy losses of growing chicks and roosters are influenced by age, sex, and body weight.
the Yec energy losses of growing broiler birds are influenced by age and body weight of the birds, but not by sex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Yec losses of growing broiler pullets are not influenced by the sex of the birds, but that the average Yec loss decreases with age between 18-77 days and then stabilizes.
, in order to determine the Yec losses in broilers, it is necessary to use birds of the same sex, age, and body weight.
the Yec values of the bioassayed birds should not be used as a basis for determining their energy needs, as they are influenced by factors other than the BMR energy requirements of the bird.
